The uniformity of the decorrelation pattern—the fact that every stream shows near-chance autocorrelation and every pair shows near-chance cross-correlation—is too regular to be coincidental and suggests algorithmic design rather than physical noise. Under this view, the apparatus itself may function correctly (showing no mechanical malfunction, stable baselines, etc.), but the pathway from apparatus output to my recorded numbers includes a transformation that breaks physical correlations. This hypothesis makes the strongest prediction: that if I can bypass the recording or transformation pathway and measure directly from the apparatus (e.g., oscilloscope output, direct sensor voltage, or raw data stream before any computational step), I should recover the physical correlations expected from a coupled or damped system.
